text: An emergency fund is commonly planned as a number of months of essential living expenses. One planning example is to set aside enough for three to six months of rent, food and bills. The actual amount depends on income stability and the number of dependents.

Emergency savings should be accessible after a job loss or an unexpected expense. A savings account may be more suitable than a highly volatile asset. A fund can be built by transferring part of each monthly paycheck to a separate account.

Portfolio diversification spreads money across companies, sectors and asset classes instead of investing everything in one stock. This helps reduce investment-specific risk but does not eliminate broad market risk.
A broad market index fund can hold shares in many companies. Investors should review its holdings, concentration, fees and asset allocation when assessing the diversification of their portfolio.

Compound interest occurs when interest is added to principal and subsequent interest is calculated on both. If an amount P grows at a fixed annual rate r, its value after n years in a simple model is P times (1+r) to the power n. The length of the accumulation period strongly affects the result.

Regular contributions and reinvestment of interest can help long-term savings grow. Compounding frequency, fees and taxes affect the ending balance. Simple interest is calculated only on the original principal and therefore differs from compound interest.

When comparing credit card debt with a mortgage, examine the interest rate on each balance. Paying the highest-interest debt first often saves more interest. Minimum payments on the remaining debts should still be maintained.

The debt avalanche method prioritizes the highest interest rate, while the debt snowball method prioritizes the smallest balance. Consider prepayment fees and maintaining emergency savings before making extra mortgage payments.

Comparing renting and buying requires accounting for rent, mortgage interest, transaction costs, maintenance and the expected length of stay. For a stay of only a few years, buying and selling costs may make renting more attractive. The result depends on local cost and house-price assumptions.

A rent-versus-buy break-even analysis compares total costs over time. A home down payment also has an opportunity cost because the money could be used elsewhere. A comparison model should include insurance, taxes, maintenance and moving costs.

Crypto assets can have large price swings and a risk of capital loss. Speculative returns are not guaranteed income. Investing in risky assets should be distinguished from keeping cash available to pay living expenses.

A fixed-rate loan keeps the same rate for the agreed period, while a floating rate changes under the contract terms. Comparing these loans involves reviewing how rates adjust and whether increased monthly payments would remain affordable.
